mainTopic: Finishing the dressing of אהרן and his sons, then why the כהן גדול leaves his wife before יום כיפור and when a בועל נדה immerses
overview: The amud opens by finishing a side discussion about whether משה dressed אהרן and his sons together or אהרן first. Each view reads the belt (אבנט) verses as teaching whether the כהן גדול's belt matched the כהן הדיוט's belt, and the two separate girding verses are shown to teach that אהרן was girded first. The גמרא then returns to the משנה's rule that the כהן גדול is separated before יום כיפור. It clarifies that its real question is why he must also leave his wife. A ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן בתירה answers: he might be with her, and afterward she might be found to be a ספק נדה, making him טמא. רב חסדא shows that this concern works even according to the רבנן, when the blood is found right after relations. רבי זירא infers from the seven-day separation that a בועל נדה may immerse by day. רב שימי rejects that proof. The גמרא then tests the question with two ברייתות, and the challenge from the second ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The 'together' view explains the two belt verses: the belts were different
steps.stepSummary: The view that אהרן and his sons were dressed together answers the earlier challenge from the two separate girding verses. The verses are separate to teach that the כהן גדול's belt differs from the כהן הדיוט's belt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could answer you: that verse comes to teach that the belt of the כהן גדול is not the same as the belt of the כהן הדיוט.
steps.whatsHappening: On the previous amud, the גמרא challenged the view that everyone was dressed together (בבת אחת). The challenge was that the Torah writes 'he girded him' and 'he girded them' as two separate verses. Here that view gives its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'together' view says the separate verses are not about order. They show that the two belts were made differently. So the split in the verses teaches a fact about the belts, not about who was dressed first.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you (introduces a defense of a position)
Belt / sash worn by the כהנים
The High Priest
An ordinary priest

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'לא זה הוא' means 'is NOT the same as.' In step 3 the wording flips to 'זהו' ('IS the same as'). The two views read the same verses as teaching opposite things about the belts.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
phrases.notes: He's defending the view that they were all dressed together.

phrases.english: That verse teaches that the belt of the High Priest

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זֶה הוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט.
phrases.english: is not the same as the belt of the ordinary priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: הַהוּא אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge earlier against the 'together' (בבת אחת) view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a different teaching (the belts differ) instead of teaching order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The separate verses seem to prove that אהרן was girded first and his sons afterward
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate verses teach that the כהן גדול's belt is different from the כהן הדיוט's belt

steps.title: Challenge to the 'Aaron first' view from 'and you shall gird them'
steps.stepSummary: Now the other view is challenged. The command verse 'וחגרת אותם אבנט' groups אהרן and his sons together, which sounds like they were girded at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says אהרן was dressed first and then his sons: isn't it written 'And you shall gird them with a belt'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side of the debate and challenges it with a verse. The verse speaks about girding 'them' all together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the command (שמות כט), the Torah says 'gird them' as one act for אהרן and his sons. That wording seems to support the 'together' view. So the 'Aaron first' view has to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to the one who says
Aaron first, and afterward his sons
But isn't it written? (introduces a challenge from a verse)

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָיו,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says: Aaron first and then his sons,
but isn't it written:
"And you shall gird them with a belt"!
phrases.notes: שמות כט:ט — one command covering everyone

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר אַהֲרֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָיו, וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel challenge: after defending the 'together' view, the גמרא now tests the opposing view
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that משה dressed אהרן first and then his sons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A single command to 'gird them' implies one combined act, which contradicts a sequential order

steps.title: The 'Aaron first' view explains the joint verse: the belts were identical
steps.stepSummary: The 'Aaron first' view answers that the joint verse teaches the כהן גדול's belt is the same as the כהן הדיוט's belt. It does not teach that the girding happened together.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could answer you: that verse teaches us that the belt of the כהן גדול is the same as the belt of the כהן הדיוט.
steps.whatsHappening: The 'Aaron first' view defends itself. The joint verse is about the material of the belts, not about the timing of the girding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By putting the belts into one command, the Torah tells us they were made the same way. The order of girding could still be אהרן first. This mirrors step 1, but with the opposite conclusion about the belts.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes to teach us
This is the same as

steps.whatToRemember: Both views turn the 'problem' verse into a teaching about the belt. The 'together' view says the belts differ. The 'Aaron first' view says the belts are identical.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָךְ: הַהוּא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: He could say to you: that verse teaches us
that the belt of the High Priest
is the same as the belt of the ordinary priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: הַהוּא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a teaching about the belt material
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Gird them' implies everyone was girded at once
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Gird them' teaches that both belts were identical; the order could still be אהרן first

steps.title: Why does the Torah need two separate girding verses?
steps.stepSummary: If the belts are identical (the 'Aaron first' view), the גמרא asks why the Torah writes girding twice: once for אהרן and once for his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need both 'and he girded him with a belt' and 'and he girded them'?
steps.whatsHappening: Still working within the 'Aaron first' view, the גמרא asks what the two separate verses in ויקרא ח are for. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'together' view used these two verses to teach that the belts differ. The 'Aaron first' view says the belts are the same, so it seems to have no use for two verses. The גמרא wants to know what this view learns from them.

keyTerms.meaning: And he girded
Why do I need it? (asks what a seemingly extra text is for)

phrases.english: "And he girded him with a belt"
phrases.notes: This is ויקרא ח:ז, talking about אהרן.

phrases.english: and "And he girded them" — why do I need both?
phrases.notes: This is ויקרא ח:יג, talking about the sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 3: if the belts are identical, the double verse needs a new purpose
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the 'Aaron first' view learns from the two separate girding verses

steps.title: The two verses teach that Aaron was girded first
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the separate verses teach the order. אהרן was girded first, then his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: אהרן first, and then his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 4. The two separate verses are the source for the 'Aaron first' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing the girding of אהרן and the girding of his sons in two different verses shows that they happened in sequence. This is exactly what the 'Aaron first' view holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a source)

phrases.english: Learn from it
that it was Aaron first, and then his sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַהֲרֹן וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two separate verses teach the order: אהרן was girded before his sons

steps.title: Could girding ever really happen 'at once'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of girding everyone 'together.' One person (משה) cannot tie several belts at the same moment, so what does 'together' even mean?
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'at once' — can you really find such a thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the whole idea of the 'together' view as it relates to girding. Physically, משה had to tie one belt at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If girding together is impossible anyway, it seems we would not need a verse to teach that אהרן came first. Some order had to exist. So the need for the two verses is challenged again.

keyTerms.meaning: At one time / simultaneously
Can you find such a case?

phrases.english: And simultaneously —
can you find such a thing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the derivation in step 5, since true simultaneity seems impossible
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a verse teaching 'Aaron first' and the meaning of the 'together' view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Girding several people at once is physically impossible, so some order is unavoidable and needs no verse

steps.title: The verse is needed to teach that Aaron came first
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the verse is needed to teach that משה started with אהרן. He then went straight on to girding the sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for the case where he put אהרן first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 6. Some order was unavoidable, but the verse teaches which order: אהרן came before his sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that girding could happen literally at once. The verse teaches that אהרן was given priority and girded first. According to the Sefaria explanation, משה then girded the sons right away, without putting other garments on אהרן in between.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (narrows the case)
That he put first / did first

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about the order and grouping of dressing אהרן and his sons. The girding verses are read either as teaching order or as teaching whether the belts were the same.

phrases.english: It is needed only
to teach that he put Aaron first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and closes the digression about dressing the כהנים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows what the verse teaches: not timing, but priority of אהרן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since simultaneous girding is impossible, the verse teaching order is unnecessary
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that אהרן specifically was girded first, followed directly by his sons

steps.title: Back to the משנה: why do we separate the כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: After the long side discussion, the גמרא returns to the משנה ('מפרישין כהן גדול') and asks why the כהן גדול is separated before יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'We separate the כהן גדול, etc.' Why do we separate him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה again to show it is going back to the main topic. It asks for the reason the כהן גדול is separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh question on the משנה after a digression. On the surface it asks for the reason behind the separation. The next step will show that this question looks strange.

keyTerms.meaning: We separate (the כהן גדול from his home before יום כיפור)
Etc. (the rest of the quoted text)

phrases.english: The משנה said: "We separate the High Priest, etc."
phrases.notes: This is quoting the very first משנה of the tractate.

phrases.english: Why do we separate him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְרִישִׁין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְכוּ׳. לָמָּה מַפְרִישִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the digression about the מילואים dressing and returns to the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for separating the כהן גדול before יום כיפור

steps.title: Surprise: we already know the reason from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the question in surprise. Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already explained where the separation comes from, so why ask?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Why do we separate him?!' It is as we said: either according to רבי יוחנן, as he holds, or according to ריש לקיש, as he holds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own question from step 8. The reason was already given earlier. This sets up the next passage, where the גמרא will explain what the question was really asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן learns the separation from the seven days of the מילואים. ריש לקיש learns it from the separation of משה at סיני. Since both sources were discussed, the plain question 'why?' seems pointless. So the question must mean something more specific.

keyTerms.meaning: As we have said
According to his own view
Learns the separation from the מילואים
Learns the separation from משה at סיני

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא physically repeats 'לָמָּה מַפְרִישִׁין' a second time. The first time is a real question. The second time is said in astonishment, challenging the first question. They are two different moves, not a typo.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to sharpen the question. In the next part it will explain that the question was about a specific detail of the separation, not about the source of the law itself.

phrases.english: "Why do we separate him?!" — what kind of question is that?
It is as we said:
either according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, as he holds,
phrases.notes: He learns it from the separation before the מילואים.

phrases.english: or according to Reish Lakish, as he holds!
phrases.notes: He learns it from the separation at סיני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question just asked in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The question 'why do we separate him' (step 8)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason was already given by both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, so the question seems unnecessary

steps.title: The real question is why he leaves his wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that its question was not where the separation comes from, but why he must leave his house, meaning his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: why did he separate from his house?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the surprise from the last step by explaining what the question really was. This sets up the next step, which gives the actual reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already explained why he is moved to a special room before יום כיפור. What they did not explain is why his wife cannot come along. 'His house' here means his wife, so the question is about her.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rewording of an earlier statement)
His house, a common way of saying 'his wife'
Separated, withdrew

steps.confusionAlert: 'מביתו' does not mean his building. In the language of the Sages, 'ביתו' usually means his wife.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Why did he separate from his house (his wife)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the surprise of step 9 by narrowing what the question of step 8 is asking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question asked for the source of the whole separation, which was already given.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question asks specifically why he must also leave his wife.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בתירה: his wife might be a ספק נדה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the reason: his wife might be found to be a doubtful נדה, and he would be with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: perhaps his wife will be found to be a doubtful נדה, and he will be with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that answers the question. He leaves his wife so that he does not become טמא through her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who is with a נדה becomes טמא for seven days. If that happened right before יום כיפור, the כהן גדול could not do the עבודה. So he stays away from her for the whole week.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
A woman whose status as a נדה is in doubt
And he will be with her (marital relations)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why he must leave his wife in particular. The seven-day length of the separation itself was already derived by רבי יוחנן (from the מילואים) and ריש לקיש (from סיני). רבי זירא will later use the match between the seven days and the seven-day טומאה of a בועל נדה.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Perhaps his wife will be found to be a doubtful niddah
and he will have relations with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarified question of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why he must separate from his wife
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To avoid becoming טמא through a wife who may be a ספק נדה

steps.title: Would a כהן גדול knowingly sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: as worded, the ברייתא pictures him knowing she is a doubtful נדה and being with her anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we dealing with wicked people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It sounds like the כהן גדול would knowingly do something forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says she is found to be a doubtful נדה first, and then he is with her. That would mean he sinned on purpose. We do not assume the כהן גדול is a רשע.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (an expression of surprise)
Wicked people
We are dealing with

phrases.english: Is that to say we are dealing with wicked people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the order of events in the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of רבי יהודה בן בתירה's reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies a deliberate sin, which we would never assume about a כהן גדול.

steps.title: Corrected order: he is with her first, then the doubt appears
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reworded. He is with his wife, and only afterward does she turn out to be a doubtful נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: perhaps he will be with his wife, and then she will be found to be a doubtful נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording by reversing the order of events. Now no one has sinned on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He was with her innocently, and afterward blood was found. That makes it doubtful whether she was already a נדה at the time. If so, he is a doubtful בועל נדה and might be טמא for seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a correction)
And she will then be found

steps.whatToRemember: The fear is not a sin. The fear is an innocent situation that turns into a doubtful טומאה afterward.

phrases.english: Rather: perhaps he will have relations with his wife
and she will then be found to be a doubtful niddah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 12 by rewording the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (reversing the order of events)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He knowingly is with a doubtful נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is with her innocently, and only afterward is she found to be a ספק נדה.

steps.title: The Sages: this reason fits only רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The Sages say before רב חסדא that this concern works only according to רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא holds that a woman found to be a נדה afterward makes the man טמא backward in time. The רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said it before רב חסדא: Whose view is this? It follows רבי עקיבא, who said a נדה makes the man who was with her טמא. Because if it followed the רבנן, they say a נדה does not make the man who was with her טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages try to identify whose opinion the ברייתא follows. They suggest it fits only רבי עקיבא and not the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי עקיבא, blood found after relations makes the man טמא backward in time. According to the רבנן, it does not. So under the רבנן, the כהן גדול would have no reason to leave his wife.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom?
Makes טמא, causes impurity
The man who was with her
Before him, in his presence

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Ḥisda:
In accordance with whom? With Rabbi Akiva,
who said: a (doubtful) niddah makes the man who was with her impure.
For if it were the Rabbis, they say:
a (doubtful) niddah does not make the man who was with her impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the corrected reason of step 13 and asks which opinion it depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The concern for a ספק נדה fits only רבי עקיבא, who holds that the man becomes טמא backward in time.

steps.title: רב חסדא: even the רבנן agree when the blood is found right after
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the limitation. The רבנן argue only when the blood was found a while later. When it was found right after, they agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: Even if you say it follows the רבנן, the רבנן disagree with רבי עקיבא only when the blood is found 'after after,' a while later. But when it is found right after, they agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back on the Sages. He shows that the ברייתא can fit the רבנן too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument between the רבנן and רבי עקיבא is limited. If blood was found a while later (אחר אחר), the רבנן say we cannot link it to the time of relations. If it was found right away (אחר), even the רבנן say the man is טמא, so the concern for the כהן גדול applies according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to this point (limits an argument)
Found a while after relations
Found right after relations
They agree

steps.whatToRemember: The reason for separating from his wife works according to everyone, because the רבנן agree when the blood is found right after relations.
steps.confusionAlert: 'אחר' versus 'אחר אחר' is about how much time passed before the blood was found. It is not about two different acts of relations.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said to them:
Even if you say it follows the Rabbis,
the Rabbis only disagree
with Rabbi Akiva
in a case of 'after after' (found a while later),
but in a case of just 'after' (found right away), they agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב חִסְדָּא: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימְרוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 14's claim that the reason fits only רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the ברייתא must follow רבי עקיבא alone
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The Sages treated the argument between רבי עקיבא and the רבנן as total, but it is limited to blood found a while later.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The concern for a ספק נדה applies according to all opinions when the blood is found right after relations.

steps.title: רבי זירא infers that a man who was with a נדה may immerse by day
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns from the seven-day separation that a בועל נדה is not like a נדה regarding the time of immersion. He may immerse during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Learn from this that a man who was with a נדה is not like the נדה herself. He may immerse during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a conclusion from the seven-day separation of the כהן גדול. He says it shows that a בועל נדה may immerse during the day, unlike a נדה, who immerses at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The separation lasts exactly seven days, which matches the seven days of טומאה of a בועל נדה. רבי זירא says this only works if the man can immerse on the seventh day itself. He explains why in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who was with a woman who is a נדה. He becomes טמא for seven days.
Learn from this (an inference).
He is not like a נדה (here, only regarding when he immerses).
He immerses during the day.

steps.confusionAlert: "Not like a נדה" here is only about WHEN he immerses. Everyone agrees he is still טמא for seven days, just like her.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Learn from it
one who had relations with a menstruating woman is not like a menstruating woman,
phrases.notes: Only regarding the timing of immersion.

phrases.english: and he immerses during the day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the now-established concern (a doubtful נדה found right after) to draw a new halachic inference about the time of immersion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בועל נדה may immerse on the seventh day during the daytime. He does not need to wait for night like a נדה.

steps.title: Why the seven-day separation proves daytime immersion
steps.stepSummary: If a בועל נדה had to immerse at night, he would immerse on the night of יום כיפור. He would still need sunset to finish becoming טהור, so he could not serve on יום כיפור. So he must be allowed to immerse by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you say a בועל נדה is like a נדה, when would he immerse? At night, which is the night of יום כיפור. Then how could he do the service the next day? He still needs to wait for sunset after immersing! So it must be that a בועל נדה is not like a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי זירא's reasoning. It shows that a night immersion would leave the כהן גדול unable to serve on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Say he was with his wife right before the separation. Then his seventh day is ערב יום כיפור. If he may immerse that day, by nightfall he is fully טהור and can serve on יום כיפור. If he had to immerse at night, he would immerse on the night of יום כיפור and would remain a טבול יום all through יום כיפור, since he must wait for הערב שמש.

keyTerms.meaning: He immerses.
At night.
Sunset after immersion. It is needed to finish becoming טהור before he may do Temple service.
The Temple service.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a practical Temple procedure, the length of the separation, can be used as evidence for a general law of טהרה.

phrases.english: For if you say that one who had relations with a menstruating woman is like a menstruating woman,
when does he immerse? At night.
phrases.notes: The night after the seventh day, which is the night of יום כיפור.

phrases.english: The next day, how can he perform the service?
But he needs sunset after his immersion!
Rather, is it not that we learn from it
that one who had relations with a menstruating woman is not like a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the proof behind רבי זירא's inference.
steps.raayaObject: That a בועל נדה immerses during the day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the כהן גדול is separated for exactly seven days, which only works if he can immerse on ערב יום כיפור by day.

steps.title: רב שימי: separate him an hour before sunset
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי מנהרדעא says there is no proof. Even if a בועל נדה immerses at night, the כהן גדול could be separated one hour before sunset. Then the seven full days end in time for a night immersion plus a day of waiting for sunset before יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי from נהרדעא said: Even if you say a בועל נדה is like a נדה, it works, because we separate the כהן גדול one hour before sunset.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי rejects רבי זירא's proof. He shows the separation can work even if a בועל נדה must immerse at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the separation starts just before sunset of the eighth day before יום כיפור, the seven full days are complete by the night that begins ערב יום כיפור. He immerses that night, waits through the day for הערב שמש, and is טהור for יום כיפור. That extra hour does not count as making the separation eight days.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say. This phrase rejects a proof by showing the other view also works.
We separate (him from his home).
Sunset.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi from Neharde'a said:
Even if you say that one who had relations with a menstruating woman is like a menstruating woman,
we separate him one hour
close to sunset.
phrases.notes: On the eighth day before יום כיפור, so that seven full days are complete in time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's proof by redefining exactly when the separation begins.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב שימי does not say רבי זירא's law is wrong. He only says the separation does not prove it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי זירא assumed the separation starts at a time that leaves no room for a night immersion. Starting it just before sunset solves that.

steps.title: A ברייתא: only a נדה and a יולדת immerse at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a בועל נדה immerses at night. A ברייתא says everyone who needs immersion does it by day, except a נדה and a יולדת. That implies a בועל נדה immerses by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection: All who are required to immerse do so by day. Only a נדה and a יולדת immerse at night. A נדה, yes; a בועל נדה, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to go against the view behind רב שימי's answer, that a בועל נדה is like a נדה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists only a נדה and a יולדת as people who immerse at night. Since a בועל נדה is not on the list, the inference is that he immerses by day, like everyone else. This backs רבי זירא's view and weakens the "even if you say" side of רב שימי's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה.
Those who are required to immerse.
A woman who has given birth.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: All those obligated in immersions
their immersion is during the day,
a menstruating woman and a woman after childbirth, their immersion is at night.
A menstruating woman, yes; one who had relations with a menstruating woman, no!
phrases.notes: This is what the ברייתא implies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the possibility, kept open by רב שימי, that a בועל נדה immerses at night like a נדה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a בועל נדה is like a נדה and immerses at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only a נדה and a יולדת as night immersers. By implication, a בועל נדה is not on the list and immerses by day.

steps.title: The word נדה includes the man who has relations with her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא. When it says a נדה immerses at night, נדה includes everyone whose impurity comes from her, including the בועל נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The term 'נדה' includes the נדה and everyone whose impurity is derived from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 19. It explains that the ברייתא's word 'נדה' is wider than it looks. It also covers the man who became impure through her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said everyone immerses by day 'except a נדה and a יולדת.' It seemed to put the בועל נדה in the 'by day' group. The answer is that a בועל נדה gets his impurity from the נדה, so he is counted under her name and follows her rule of night immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had relations with a נדה and so becomes impure for seven days
Who comes from an inclusion, meaning someone included in her status
A woman after childbirth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the בועל נדה actually is a נדה. He keeps his own category. He only follows her rule for the timing of immersion because his impurity is derived from hers.

phrases.english: 'A menstruating woman' includes her and everyone who comes from her inclusion.
phrases.notes: The בועל נדה gets his impurity from her, so he is included in her rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term in the ברייתא (widening its scope)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'נדה' means only the woman herself, so the בועל נדה immerses by day.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נדה' includes everyone whose impurity derives from her, so the בועל נדה also immerses at night.

steps.title: A new ברייתא compares the בועל נדה to a טמא מת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a בעל קרי is like one who touched a שרץ, and a בועל נדה is like a טמא מת. The גמרא suggests this means the בועל נדה immerses by day, like a טמא מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: A בעל קרי is like one who touched a שרץ, and a בועל נדה is like a טמא מת. Doesn't this refer to immersion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge the idea that a בועל נדה immerses at night. If he is compared to a טמא מת, who immerses by day, then he should also immerse by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא מת is not a נדה or יולדת, so he immerses by day. The phrase 'מאי לאו' suggests the comparison is about the time of immersion. If so, the בועל נדה would immerse by day, against the view being defended.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged; introduces a source brought as an objection
A man who had a seminal emission
Contact with a creeping creature, which causes one-day impurity
Someone made impure by a dead body, with seven-day impurity
Is it not? Introduces a suggested reading of a source
Immersion in a מקוה

phrases.english: They challenged: one who had a seminal emission is like one who touched a creeping creature,
one who had relations with a menstruating woman is like one impure from a corpse.
Is it not referring to immersion?
phrases.notes: A טמא מת immerses by day, so the בועל נדה would too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 20 defended night immersion, a new source is brought against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a בועל נדה immerses at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא equates the בועל נדה with a טמא מת. A טמא מת immerses by day, so if the comparison is about immersion, the בועל נדה immerses by day too.

steps.title: The comparison is only about how long they are impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא compares the length of impurity, not the time of immersion. A בעל קרי is impure for one day like one who touched a שרץ. A בועל נדה is impure for seven days like a טמא מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it refers to their impurity, meaning how long it lasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from Step 21. The ברייתא is only comparing how long each person stays impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two people can be alike in one way and different in another. The ברייתא matches the בועל נדה to a טמא מת only in the seven-day length. It says nothing about when he immerses, so night immersion is still possible.

keyTerms.meaning: Their impurity; here, its length

phrases.english: No, it refers to their impurity.
phrases.notes: Meaning the length: one day versus seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 21 by limiting what the comparison is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא compares the בועל נדה to a טמא מת for the time of immersion (by day).
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא compares only the length of impurity (seven days).

steps.title: The length of their impurity is already written in the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The seven-day impurity of both the טמא מת and the בועל נדה is written openly in the Torah, so why would a ברייתא need to compare them for that? The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their impurity?! It is written openly about them. This one has seven-day impurity written about him, and that one has seven-day impurity written about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 22. A ברייתא would not need to teach something the Torah already says plainly. This sets up the rest of the argument on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah states seven days for a טמא מת (במדבר י״ט) and for a בועל נדה (ויקרא ט״ו). Since each one's length is already stated, comparing them for length teaches nothing new. That suggests the ברייתא must be about something else, such as immersion.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, explicitly
It is written in the Torah
Seven-day impurity

phrases.english: Their impurity?! It is explicitly written about them.
This one (the corpse-impure) has seven-day impurity written about him,
and that one (the one who had relations with a menstruating woman) has seven-day impurity written about him,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues into the next passage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא compares only the length of impurity.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both seven-day lengths are explicit in the Torah. A ברייתא would not bother comparing two things that are each already written, so the comparison must teach something else.
